title: Observation of Gravitational Waves from the Coalescence of a 2.5–4.5 M⊙ Compact Object and a Neutron Star
extended_summary:
This paper reports the detection and astrophysical interpretation of the gravitational-wave event GW230529 181500, observed during the fourth observing run of the LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA network. The authors focus on estimating the properties of the compact binary source, including component masses, and on assessing whether the primary object is more likely a neutron star or a black hole.

The study is based on gravitational-wave observations from LIGO Livingston, with no educational intervention, instructional tool, or learner population involved. The analysis uses detector data and astrophysical modeling to infer source characteristics such as mass range, possible merger type, and merger-rate implications.

The main conclusion is that GW230529 likely represents a neutron star–black hole merger, though the data do not definitively identify the nature of either component. The event provides evidence for compact objects in the lower mass gap between the heaviest neutron stars and lightest black holes, and it suggests that similar systems may contribute substantially to the population of neutron star–black hole mergers.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is an astrophysics research article on gravitational-wave observation, not an education study. It contains no K-12 intervention, comparator, or student outcome methodology relevant to the requested taxonomy.
